pool.text: Immigrants speaking the Duala language formed a town in the area.
Douala consisted of four distinct villages located in specific geographic locations.
Alfred Saker organized the first mission of the British Baptist Church.
Terracotta bricks began to be produced within the city of Douala.
A first urban plan of the city was developed during German rule.
Construction of the Villa Mandessi Bell began in the city.
The palace of the King Manga Ndumbe Bell was built in Douala.
The Ministry of Colonies was established while Douala held citizens.
The large population living in Bonanjo moved to Neue Bell.
The Mausoleum of the Kings Akwa was constructed in Douala.
Douala served as the capital of Cameroon during this period.
The Temple of the Centenary was built in the city.
The bridge on Wouri River was built in the city.
A new city plan named Plan Dorian was designed for Douala.
Cameroon gained independence as a federal republic with Yaoundé capital.
Douala was the center of the civil disobedience campaign ghost town.
A new development and urban plan was designed in Douala.
La Nouvelle Liberté by Joseph Francis Sumégné was inaugurated.
Many Douala inhabitants knew how to read, write, and speak French.
The city and surrounding area estimated population reached millions.
